nodes.label: AppDbContext (EF Core)
nodes.rationale: Targets SQL Server via Microsoft.Data.SqlClient; UseSqlOutputClause(false) is required on tables with triggers.

nodes.label: Gemini AI Integration (IGeminiService)
nodes.rationale: Configured via GeminiSettings bound from appsettings.json; accessed only through the IGeminiService interface.

nodes.label: Image Upload Services (ImageService / IImageService)
nodes.rationale: Image uploads are handled by ImageService registered as a Singleton (explicit exception to the Scoped-by-default DI rule) plus scoped IImageService / ImageUploadService.

nodes.label: ItemModel
nodes.rationale: ItemModel uses RequestItemID as its primary key — an intentional, documented exception to the RequestID primary key rule.

nodes.label: location_update Rider Payload
nodes.rationale: Direct rider payload with Type=location_update carrying RequestID, RiderId, Latitude/Longitude, Timestamp, Status, RiderInitial, ETA, Distance, and Client; the server rebroadcasts it wrapped as Message=Location and excludes the sender from its own broadcast.

nodes.label: Notification Broadcast Payload
nodes.rationale: Wrapped Message=Notification payloads deliver Title and Body to other connected clients.

nodes.label: WebSocket Endpoint /api/ws
nodes.rationale: Production clients connect via wss://<host>/api/ws?apiKey=<key>; connections with a missing or invalid apiKey are rejected, and malformed JSON is logged as a warning without dropping the connection so the client can send the next valid message.

nodes.label: Scoped DI Registration in Program.cs
nodes.rationale: All services and repositories are registered as Scoped in Program.cs unless there is an explicit reason for Singleton (e.g., ImageService).

nodes.label: Custom ID Generators (Counter Tables)
nodes.rationale: Custom ID generators (RequestIdGenerator, ItemIdGenerator, etc.) use counter tables; new generators must follow the existing pattern.

nodes.label: Repository Pattern
nodes.rationale: Data access is abstracted behind I*Repository interfaces in Core and implemented in Data, so services can be unit tested by mocking repositories via their interfaces.

nodes.label: RequestID Primary Key Rule
nodes.rationale: Use RequestID as primary key on Items and related tables; do not introduce a separate RequestItemID unless there is a documented need for item-level identity independent of the request. For multiple items per request use composite key (RequestID, ItemIndex) or a justified surrogate; schemas that already have RequestItemID should consolidate onto RequestID. ItemModel is an intentional exception that keeps RequestItemID as its primary key.

nodes.label: Service Pattern
nodes.rationale: Business logic lives in Core/Services classes implementing I*Service interfaces, keeping controllers thin and logic testable.

nodes.label: WebSocket API Key Authentication
nodes.rationale: The production key is supplied via configuration (preferably the WebSocket__ApiKey environment-style setting) rather than hardcoded; missing or invalid keys cause connection rejection.

nodes.label: Clean Architecture Pattern
nodes.rationale: Dependency direction Api -> Core <- Data keeps Core free of references to Data or Api; Data implements interfaces defined in Core so business logic stays independent of infrastructure.

nodes.label: Domain-First Folder Structure
nodes.rationale: Code is organized by domain area first (Common, Logistic, Collection) and then by concern, across Core, Data, and Api/Controllers.
